name: pattern-matching-cep
context: A business event is only recognizable after several events have occurred, in a specific order, within a bounded time span — 'order created, then payment declined, then customer cancelled, all within 10 minutes'. Complex Event Processing declares that sequence as a pattern over a stream keyed by the correlation key and emits a match when the pattern completes, or a timed-out partial match when it does not. Contiguity between successive elements is explicit: strict ('must immediately follow'), relaxed ('other events may intervene'), or non-deterministic relaxed ('emit every possible match').
benefits: Turns an implicit business condition scattered across many ad-hoc consumers into one declarable, testable pattern definition
Emits matches rather than state snapshots, so downstream only sees the interesting outcomes
Partial matches can be surfaced with a timeout handler, making 'started but never completed' observable instead of silent
Event-time constraints make detection deterministic with respect to data rather than arrival jitter
Looping constructs (optional, oneOrMore, times) express variable-length sequences without hand-rolled counters
tradeoffs: Pattern state grows with the number of distinct in-flight partial matches per key, and is never garbage collected until a match completes or times out
Non-deterministic relaxed contiguity plus looping patterns can emit a combinatorial number of matches for the same starting event
Correctness depends on the input being keyed by the correlation key — a pattern can never match across keys, so cross-entity sequences are impossible
Tuned lateness inflates memory and state churn; tuned tightly it silently drops late-arriving matches
Detection adds latency: the pattern cannot fire before the last element of the sequence arrives
use_cases: Fraud scoring on card-not-present sequences (stolen credential followed by high-value order)
Order lifecycle monitoring: created, then payment failed, then abandoned within the configured timeout
Network and security telemetry: repeated failed logins followed by a successful login from a new address
IoT condition monitoring: three consecutive over-temperature readings within five minutes
Clickstream funnel detection: view -> add to cart -> purchase within a session-like timeout
avoid_when: The condition is a single stateless predicate on one record — that is a filter, not a pattern
A count over a time window expresses the requirement — use windowing instead of contiguity tracking
The correlation key is not known at design time and cannot be derived from the record
The sequence is unbounded in length and never terminates — no finite pattern can express it
component_types: Pattern: a graph of simple patterns joined by contiguity operators (begin, next, followedBy, followedByAny)
Condition: per-pattern predicate, optionally iterative so it can reference previously matched events or accumulated state
Time constraint: 'within' bound bounding the total span of a match in event time or processing time
Pattern stream: the keyed input stream paired with the pattern and an optional timestamp comparator
Process function: callback invoked per match, receiving a map from pattern name to the accepted events
Timeout handler: optional callback for partial sequences discarded by the time constraint
anti_patterns: Using relaxed contiguity with an unbounded oneOrMore loop, producing one match per permutation of the sequence
Matching on a stream that is not keyed by the correlation key, which silently yields zero matches
Leaving 'within' unset, so partial matches accumulate forever and state never drains
Building CEP over the hot transactional path instead of over a derived, replayable alert topic
Assuming a match is delivered once — the same sequence can match again on replay of the same input
design_principles: Declaration over imperative correlation: the sequence is described, not coded
Explicit contiguity: every transition states whether intervening events break the match
Boundedness: every pattern carries a time constraint so partial state is always drainable
Key locality: detection is per correlation key, so state is bounded by in-flight entities
Partial visibility: unfinished sequences are observable, not silently discarded
best_practices: Start with strict contiguity and relax only when real production traffic proves the relaxed form necessary
Derive the correlation key explicitly and assert it upstream — a null key means a permanently dead pattern
Size the time constraint from observed inter-arrival distributions, not from a round number
Cap match cardinality: use skip-till-next-match semantics where overlapping matches are meaningless
Emit matches to a dedicated topic so the pattern itself stays replayable and independently testable
